span.label: pupil derivative → pupil diameter
span.note: THE INDEXING / PROXY RELATION - Q-299. `from` STANDS IN FOR `to`. We have no type for it: `causes` asserts production, and `operationalised-as` says the authors CHOSE a measure, whereas a proxy claim says THIS STANDS IN FOR WHAT WE ACTUALLY CARE ABOUT AND WE KNOW IT IS NOT THE SAME THING. Measured at 8% of papers. A PROXY FOR ITSELF, DISPLACED IN TIME: 'the explanatory power of the pupil derivative occurs because IT SERVES AS A PROXY FOR THE PUPIL DIAMETER APPROXIMATELY 1 SECOND LATER'. The two endpoints are the same measurement at different lags, which is a substitution no vocabulary of concepts would catch.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: RETRACTED (THE FIELD'S DISAGREEMENT, PLUS THE VIEW THIS PAPER COMPLICATES) · state —causes→ membrane potential
span.note: RETRACTED: THE FIELD'S DISAGREEMENT, PLUS THE VIEW THIS PAPER COMPLICATES. The span: 'Reports on the cortical membrane potential dynamics associated with wakeful states Quotation withheld. Wakefulness is TRADITIONALLY ASSOCIATED with low amplitude and arrhythmic scalp EEG. THIS CANONICAL...' - the first sentence says the literature does not agree and the second states the canonical view. The paper's own finding is that the relationship is non-monotonic in arousal, which is why the canonical account is quoted here at all. A reader joining on `X --causes--> Y` takes it as a causal relation this paper reports. Q-395. — strength of the relation: 1 — and the reports it is meant to reconcile came to widely differing conclusions between species and sensory systems

span.label: pupil —contrasted-with→ derivative
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS WHICH PREDICTOR ADDS ANYTHING, AND THE ANSWER IS THAT ONE DOES NOT. 'FACTORING IN BOTH THE PUPIL DIAMETER AND ITS DERIVATIVE explained 40+/-6% of the variance of power in the 2-10 Hz band, WHICH WAS STATISTICALLY LARGER THAN THE AMOUNT EXPLAINED BY PUPIL DERIVATIVE (p<0.0005), BUT NOT PUPIL DIAMETER ALONE (p=0.36).' Adding the derivative to diameter does not improve on diameter alone - a null reported in the same sentence as the significant comparison, and the pair is only distinguishable because both tests are given. Q-473. · strength of the relation: 1 — A RIVAL MEASURE TESTED HEAD TO HEAD: the diameter explains 34 percent of the variance in low-frequency power, the derivative about half that, and both together add nothing over the diameter alone

span.label: derivative —distinct-from→ pupil
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS TEMPORAL LAG, AND BOTH CORRELATIONS ARE GIVEN. 'THE DERIVATIVE OF THE PUPIL WAS CORRELATED TO THE PUPIL DIAMETER 1.3 +/- 0.7 SECONDS LATER (CC = 0.32 +/- 0.02; p<0.001), BUT NOT TO THE PUPIL DIAMETER AT THE SAME TIME (CC = 0.0035 +/- 0.0043; p=0.44).' The same two quantities are unrelated at lag zero and strongly related at 1.3 s - so a study measuring them concurrently would report independence, and the paper goes on to attribute the lag to muscle and neural delays in pupil control. Q-473. · strength of the relation: 1 — AND THEN EXPLAINED AWAY: the derivative correlates with the diameter 1.3 s later and not with the diameter at the same moment, so some and perhaps all of its power is borrowed

span.note: RETRACTED: THE PAPER IS PULLING THESE TWO APART AND THE EDGE JOINS THEM. The edge is `movement --renamed-across-fields--> arousal`. The span: 'the often reported effects of movement Quotation withheld.' That is a re-attribution of a cause, not a renaming of a term - and the sentence after it NAMES THE CASE WHERE THE TWO COME APART: 'with THE EXCEPTION OF an arousal-independent walking effect on thalamic sound responses and decision bias.' A `renamed-across-fields` edge says the two labels denote the same thing, which deletes exactly that exception. WHAT THE SPAN DOES SAY (Q-309): that in these animals walking necessarily involved strong arousal, so the two were confounded by the design, and the effects previously attributed to movement track arousal instead - except for one effect that does not. — strength of the relation: 1 — A LITERATURE'S INDEPENDENT VARIABLE RE-IDENTIFIED: the often reported effects of movement may not result from movement per se but from arousal - with one arousal-independent walking effect on thalamic responses and bias named and kept
